correctness.rationale: The stationary convolution is well defined by positive on-state occupation. For integer n>=1 the killed two-state generator Q-2n*kappa*diag(0,1) has negative trace and positive determinant; the L^n norm of the exponential integrand of the conditional variance thus decays exponentially with lag. Minkowski integration gives finite variance-mixture moments of every finite order, and synchronous coupling contracts since the integrated on-time diverges. The stationary state-resolved moments solve a nonsingular 2-by-2 system with M1=D/kappa and M0=(2D*pi0+beta M1)/alpha. The lagged generator has characteristic polynomial p(z)=z^2-(kappa+T)z+alpha*kappa with p(0)>0 and p(kappa)<0. C(0)=V and C'(0+)=-D fix the two displayed residues. At s=D/V<kappa, p(s) has the sign of H by the exact factorization, so A+ has the opposite sign while A->0. A negative fast coefficient violates high-order alternating derivative signs, since lambda+>lambda-. Twice differentiating or using the lag generator gives C''(0+)=D*kappa*(alpha-beta)/T; dividing C''(t) by the positive slow exponential reduces it to a constant plus a single decaying term. This validates all three curvature cases including alpha=beta and the strict crossing for alpha<beta. For H=0 the remaining mode has rate T/2 and variance 2D/T. The fourth moment equations give N1=3DV/kappa, N0=(12DM0+beta N1)/alpha and hence the positive fourth cumulant and standardized excess in the frozen claim. The independent script python3 /workspace/review_replay.py (section 5) corroborates the exact stationary moment and phase identities on 21 rational cases. The frozen checker was inspected but not executed; it applies five lag comparisons to 1,029 grid cases, then 21 extra cancellation checks, not five lag comparisons for all 1,050. This does not affect the proof.

value.rationale: An unconfined phase is a natural physical boundary, and the interpretation of OU covariance with a non-Gaussian marginal is useful. But as a standalone research contribution, the main camouflage classification and its diagnostic reduce to the existing regular two-stiffness formulas, and the residual sign and curvature observations are obtained by evaluating the same known two-mode ODE and comparing its two exponential terms. No new diagnostic, exact invariant beyond the existing solution, or singular-boundary obstruction giving independent mathematical value was established. No substantive repair is claimed.
